explanations: luna: The section's lexical image is explicit here: earth is made a “فِرَاشًا” and sky a “بِنَاءً”; rain and fruit in the same verse make this roof-and-floor a provisioned human dwelling. | terra: Earth as فِرَاشًا and heaven as بِنَاءً are the section's floor and roof in the Quran's own explicit domestic wording.

luna: After creating what is on earth, God turns to the sky and “فَسَوَّاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ”; this uses the section's finishing verb for the heavens themselves. | terra: After creating what is on earth, God turns to heaven and فَسَوَّاهُنَّ as seven heavens, joining the lower realm to a divinely finished upper structure.
terra: God shades Israel with الْغَمَامَ and supplies food, showing an overhead covering functioning as merciful shelter.
luna: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations; this human construction gives a specific counterpart to the section's cosmic house built from upper roof and lower surface.
terra: The command to look at the bones as God raises or assembles them and then clothes them with flesh directly stages the rebuilding of the human frame.

luna: “يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ” locates the shaping of human forms in the womb, a concrete setting for the section's formed human structure. | terra: God forms human beings in the wombs however He wills, a direct Quranic statement of the divine fashioning behind the section's third structure.
terra: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ gives the section's statement that every human is a nafs its universal mortal boundary.
terra: Humanity is created from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ and its mate, using nafs as the single human self from which a living population is built.
terra: At death the command أَخْرِجُوا أَنْفُسَكُمُ separates the selves from bodily life, supporting the section's living-spirit sense of nafs.
terra: أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ links being brought into existence with the section's claim that each human is a nafs.

luna: “خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَاكُمْ” gives a creation-then-forming sequence for human beings, parallel to the section's formed nafs. | terra: “We created you, then shaped you” makes human form the deliberate result of divine workmanship.
terra: The cloud again shades the people in the wilderness, a concrete instance of the section's "what rises above and shades you" definition.
terra: The mountain is raised above the people كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ and they fear it will fall; an overhead canopy becomes a threatening reversal of the protective, shading roof.
terra: God creates people from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ and makes its mate from it, another direct use of nafs as an originating human self.

luna: The Qur'an describes a building founded on piety versus one on a crumbling bank; read beside the section's formed nafs, it gives a specific moral extension to its house image. | terra: A building founded on reverence is set against one on a collapsing bank that falls with its builder into fire; construction becomes an exact image of the soul's moral foundation and possible ruin.
terra: The building of 9:109 remains a source of doubt “in their hearts” until those hearts are cut, carrying the outer construction into the inward human structure.
terra: أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَاسْتَعْمَرَكُمْ فِيهَا makes humans from the house's floor and appoints them to inhabit and cultivate it.

luna: God “رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا”: the raised roof has no visible pillars, clarifying how its construction differs from a tent's supports. | terra: God raises the heavens بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا; the roof is explicitly architectural while its lack of visible pillars marks a boundary with the section's tent-poles and bodily ribs.

luna: “مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ” is a direct spread-earth formulation; its rivers and fixed mountains specify features placed on that surface. | terra: وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ directly restages the section's act of spreading the lower surface.
terra: The day earth is replaced by another earth and the heavens as well marks the temporal boundary of the present floor-and-roof arrangement.
terra: Constellations are placed in heaven and it is beautified for viewers, another direct depiction of the roof as intentionally finished and adorned.
terra: وَحَفِظْنَاهَا follows the adorned heaven of 15:16 with protection from every expelled devil.
terra: The exception of a listener pursued by a visible flame shows how the guarding asserted in 15:17 actively repels an attempted breach of the adorned heaven.

luna: “مَدَدْنَاهَا” directly describes the earth spread out, then mentions mountains and measured growth upon it, extending the floor image. | terra: Earth is مَدَدْنَاهَا and its growth is مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَوْزُونٍ; the spread floor and measured fitness appear in one scene.

luna: The human is proportioned and receives spirit: “سَوَّيْتُهُ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي,” the same body-and-life pairing as the section's nafs definition. | terra: God's command follows فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ with breathing into the human from His spirit, directly coupling the finished structure with life.
luna: Firm mountains are placed lest earth sway with people; this is a functional parallel to the section's tent pegs fixing the ground.
terra: God strikes a hostile building at its foundations so its roof falls on its occupants from above, a direct structural reversal of the protected roof over a secure floor.

luna: The verse calls portable livestock-skin dwellings “بُيُوتًا”; this is the section's secondary dictionary image of a domed tent made from hides. | terra: Houses from animal hides and furnishings from wool, camel hair, and hair are the Quranic realization of the section's leather tent and wool-or-camel-hair floor covering.

luna: God makes “ظِلَالًا” and mountain shelters; this fits the section's named secondary sense of sky as what rises over and shades you. | terra: God makes ظِلَالًا from created things immediately after the hide-tents of 16:80, realizing the section's definition of an overhead structure by the shade it gives.
luna: The section's dictionary form glosses nafs as the living body's rūḥ; this verse sets an epistemic boundary around “الرُّوحُ,” calling it of the Lord's command and human knowledge little.

luna: The verse argues that the Creator of heavens and earth can create people again; it extends the section's sky-versus-human creation challenge to resurrection. | terra: Creation of the heavens and earth is the stated proof that God can create human beings again, joining the outer house to the maker of its mortal occupants.

luna: The speaker challenges denial by recalling creation from dust, then a drop, then formation as a man; it is another concrete human-formation argument beside the section's sky-versus-human comparison.

luna: Mountains are moved and the earth laid bare; this reverses the section's pegged landscape and spread, habitable ground. | terra: Mountains are removed and the earth is left exposed and level, dismantling the peg-and-floor arrangement used by the section's tent image.
luna: The root س و ي is used as “سَاوَى” for leveling between two mountain sides while building a barrier, a second concrete scene of construction and leveling.
terra: The Lord gives each thing its خلق and then guides it, a nonlexical parallel to making a created structure fit for its mode of life.

luna: The earth is made “مَهْدًا” and routes are opened in it; the verse depicts a habitable ground under the sky, as in the section's floor image. | terra: God makes earth مَهْدًا for the addressees, presenting the ground as an inhabitable bedding.
luna: After earth is called a bed in 20:53, this verse directs people to eat from it and pasture their livestock, making its inhabitable surface concrete.
terra: Humans are created from earth, returned to it, and brought from it again, tying the living structure materially and temporally to the floor beneath it.
luna: The mountains used as tent pegs in 78:7 are here destined to be scattered; this verse begins the reversal of their anchoring role.

luna: After mountains are questioned in 20:105, this verse says they are left level, undoing their peg-like fixing of the earth. | terra: God leaves the mountains as a level plain, turning the structural fixtures of the inhabited earth into an unfeatured final surface.

luna: The next verse completes the leveled landscape: no crookedness or rise remains where mountains had served as anchors. | terra: No depression or rise remains in the plain of 20:106, defining the total leveling that replaces the present fitted floor.
luna: The section defines earth as the body opposite the sky; this verse reverses that distinction at the origin by saying heaven and earth were joined and then parted.
luna: Firm mountains are set in earth lest it shake, another explicit stabilizing role that sharpens the tent-peg image.

luna: “السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا مَّحْفُوظًا” directly names the sky as a protected roof, the section's central gloss for the upper structure. | terra: سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا names heaven itself as a protected roof, the section's central architectural identification.

luna: At the final boundary, the sky is rolled up like a written scroll; this gives a distinct reversal of the section's erected roof. | terra: God will roll heaven like a written scroll and repeat creation as He began it, setting the roof's dismantling beside the Builder's power to rebuild.

luna: In an argument about resurrection, this verse sets stages of human formation beside rain reviving dead earth; it brings the section's formed person and spread ground into one scene. | terra: مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ distinguishes formed from unformed embryonic substance and traces it to mature human life, exposing the process behind the finished structure.

luna: God holds the sky from falling on earth; this gives the roof image a specific account of how the upper structure is kept over the ground. | terra: God holds heaven back from falling on earth except by His leave, dramatizing how the overhead roof is sustained above the floor.
terra: Human creation begins from an extract of clay, the first material step in the assembled bodily scene completed at 23:14.
terra: The drop is placed in قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ, a secure lodging that immediately precedes the successive construction of 23:14.

luna: Bones are clothed with flesh before a new creation; this gives a specific assembly of bodily parts behind the section's “building by joining parts” gloss. | terra: Bones are made and clothed with flesh before أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ; this staged assembly makes the living human a structure whose parts precede a further creation.
terra: God creates seven ways above the audience and is not heedless of creation, presenting the upper structure as layered and continuously attended.
terra: God creates everything and فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا, stating precise determination as the order behind formed creation.
terra: The day heaven splits with cloud and angels descend turns the overhead expanse into an opened boundary rather than a closed roof.

luna: The section explicitly gives the lexicographic gloss “what rises above and shades you”; this verse stages an extended “ظِلّ” as that covering. | terra: God extends the shade and makes the sun its guide, developing the source section's secondary definition of an overhead expanse through the shade it casts.

luna: After 25:45 extends shade, this verse says it is gradually drawn back; its own contribution is the withdrawal that qualifies shade as a changing cover. | terra: God then draws the shade in gradually, showing that the canopy's shading effect is itself measured and governed.
terra: عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ turns the very image of a shade-canopy into the setting of punishment rather than shelter.

luna: The verse asks who made earth a settled abode and placed rivers and mountains within it; this is a distinct formulation of the section's inhabitable ground beneath the sky. | terra: The earth is made a stable dwelling with rivers, mountains, and barriers, elaborating how the lower part of the house is secured for life.
luna: Mountains that seem fixed pass like clouds; this reverses their peg-like stability and shows the ground image at the judgment boundary.
luna: Pharaoh orders a tower of baked clay to look toward Moses' God; this is a human-built, earth-bound counter-image to the divine construction of the sky.

luna: The spider's house is called the weakest house; the verse is about false protectors, so its connection is only a boundary case for the section's built, protected cosmic dwelling. | terra: The spider's house is called the frailest of houses, giving the God-built and protected cosmic dwelling a concrete opposite in a structure unable to protect its occupant.
terra: Human beings are created from dust and then spread abroad as people, making the inhabitants arise from the material of the floor on which they move.
terra: Heaven and earth stand by God's command, and the same voice will call human beings out from earth, joining the house's stability to its occupants' renewed life.

luna: The section's dictionary gloss connects sound human “بِنْيَة” with fitra; this verse explicitly names God's “فِطْرَتَ” upon which people are created. | terra: The source dictionary explicitly glosses sound binya as fiṭra; فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا names that God-given native constitution.

luna: This pairs heavens “بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ” with firm mountains placed in earth; it contrasts the unsupported upper structure with the pegged, stabilized ground. | terra: Heaven is created without visible pillars and mountains are cast into earth to steady it, pairing a supportless roof with a stabilized floor.
terra: Human creation and resurrection are كَنَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ, making the single nafs the measure of how effortlessly the Builder can form all people.

terra: The same surah's account of fashioning and breathing life into the human at 32:7-9 begins by naming God as Creator of the heavens, earth, and what lies between, reinforcing the single-Builder sequence.
terra: God makes good everything He creates and begins human creation from clay, supplying the rule of workmanship behind the fashioned, ensouled human of 32:9.
terra: The human line is made from an extract of fluid before the fashioning and breath of 32:9, contributing the material stage of the third structure.

luna: The section's third structure is a living human: “سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِ” joins proportioning the body with the spirit that gives it life. | terra: ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِهِ joins divine fashioning to the breath that makes the body live, matching the section's definition of nafs as its living spirit.

terra: The audience is told to see the heaven and earth enclosing them, then warned that earth can swallow them or a piece of heaven fall, exposing the two boundaries of the cosmic house as possible agents of collapse.
terra: Human formation from dust and then a drop, followed by pairing, gestation, birth, and measured lifespan, traces both the material assembly and temporal measure of the living structure.

luna: God holds the heavens and earth lest they cease; the verse ties the two structures in the section's house image to God's sustaining act. | terra: God holds the heavens and earth from ceasing or slipping away, presenting continued preservation as part of their construction.
terra: The objector displays decayed bones and asks who can give them life, bringing the dismantled bodily frame and loss of its living principle into one challenge.

luna: The reply to the question about dead bones says the One who originated them first can revive them; 36:81 then supplies the sky-and-earth proof, while this row contributes the first-creation premise. | terra: The answer to 36:78 is that the One who originated the bones the first time will revive them, identifying their original Builder as their rebuilder.

luna: The argument from making the heavens and earth to the ability to create humans again directly develops the resurrection challenge cited in the section's 79:27 sequence. | terra: The Creator of the heavens and earth is asked whether He can create the like of human beings, making cosmic building evidence for rebuilding the person.
terra: إِنَّا زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا adorns the nearest heaven with stars, matching the section's built and decorated ceiling.
terra: وَحِفْظًا مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَارِدٍ adds guarding to the adorned heaven of 37:6, spelling out its protected-roof function.

luna: This account likewise says “فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ” before breathing the spirit into the human; it makes the formed person a living structure. | terra: The repeated Adam scene again places divine breathing after سَوَّيْتُهُ, confirming the section's link between a formed body and its living inward principle.
terra: Creation from نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ leads to human creation stage after stage within three darknesses, joining the living self to a nested work of construction.
luna: “غُرَفٌ مِّن فَوْقِهَا غُرَفٌ مَّبْنِيَّةٌ” pictures built rooms above rooms; it offers a specific stacked-house parallel to the section's image of the nafs as a third room.

luna: The section glosses nafs as the spirit by which the body lives; this verse says God takes the “الْأَنفُسَ” in sleep and death, showing the soul-body relation at its boundary. | terra: God takes الْأَنْفُسَ at death and in sleep, retaining some and returning others; this directly tests the section's dictionary definition of nafs by bodily life and its cessation.
terra: The heavens will be folded in God's right hand, reversing the section's image of the presently extended overhead structure.
luna: Pharaoh orders Haman “ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا,” a human tower-building counter-scene to the sky built by God; 40:37 specifies the intended reach toward heaven.
terra: The creation of heavens and earth is declared greater than creating humankind, directly comparing the cosmic structure with the human one as 79:27 does.

luna: “الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً” gives the paired ground and structure, then says God “صَوَّرَكُمْ”; the formed human completes the section's three-part house. | terra: This ayah states the section's whole three-part architecture at once: earth is a settled floor, heaven is بِنَاءً, and God fashions human forms beautifully.
terra: The ayah traces human beings through dust, drop, clot, childhood, strength, age, and death, showing the built self as a staged and time-bounded formation.

luna: This earth-creation verse places firm mountains above the ground and apportions its provisions; after 41:9 and before the sky's completion in 41:11–12, it adds a stabilized, provisioned lower structure.

terra: During creation God addresses heaven while it is smoke and commands heaven and earth to come; their joint willing response presents roof and floor as paired participants before 41:12 completes the heavens.

luna: After the heavens are formed in 41:11, this verse makes seven skies and adorns the lowest with lamps; it gives a concrete continuation of the constructed upper realm. | terra: God completes the seven heavens, assigns each its order, adorns the nearest with lamps, and protects it; construction, fitting, decoration, and guarding coincide.
terra: Creation of the heavens and earth is joined to living creatures dispersed through them and God's power to gather them, linking the cosmic structure, its lives, and their reassembly.

luna: “جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ مَهْدًا” directly pictures the earth as a laid-out cradle or bed for people. | terra: Earth is made مَهْدًا and furnished with ways, so the section's floor is shown as fitted for those living on it.

luna: This asks whether the One who created the heavens and earth can revive the dead, making cosmic construction evidence for human re-creation as in 79:27. | terra: The One who created the heavens and earth without fatigue is declared able to revive the dead, so cosmic construction warrants restoration of the living structure.

luna: The verse asks how God built and adorned the sky, then says it has no “فُرُوجٍ”; this is the section's roof with no cracks. | terra: The sky is بَنَيْنَاهَا, adorned, and without fissures, giving the section's roof both construction and finished integrity.

luna: After the built sky in 50:6, this verse says “مَدَدْنَاهَا” of earth and places mountains and growth on it; its own contribution is the lower spread plane. | terra: The earth is extended immediately after the intact built sky of 50:6, completing that passage's floor beneath the roof.
luna: Continuing the sky-and-earth scene after 50:7, this verse sends blessed water from the sky and grows gardens and grain; it connects the roof above to growth on the spread ground.
luna: The same scene continues with tall date palms and layered fruit; its own contribution is growth rising from the earth described in 50:7.
luna: This continuation calls the yield provision and says water revives a dead town; it links the spread earth to both sustenance and resurrection.

luna: The section names the building root ب ن ي for the sky; “بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ” directly stages God's construction of it. | terra: وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا presents God directly as the powerful builder of the section's upper structure.

luna: The section's earth-floor image is explicit in “فَرَشْنَاهَا”; following 51:47, this verse supplies the lower, spread surface of the same cosmic house. | terra: Beside the built heaven of 51:47, وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا makes earth the spread furnishing beneath it.
luna: Immediately before the section's quoted raised roof in 52:5 stands the “الْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ”; this row supplies the inhabited-house image beside the ceiling.

luna: “السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ” is the raised roof invoked in an oath, directly matching the section's sky-as-ceiling definition. | terra: The oath by السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ names the sky as the raised ceiling over the cosmic house.
terra: In the surah that swears by the raised roof at 52:5, heaven will later sway violently, exposing the constructed order's final limit.
terra: God knows people both when He brings them from earth and when they are embryos in their mothers, directly linking the cosmic floor's material with the hidden formation of the human occupant.
terra: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ generalizes measured creation, illuminating the balance and fitness carried by سَوَّاهَا.

luna: “السَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ” joins the raised roof to balance; this makes cosmic structure and proportion co-present as in the section's account of sawwā. | terra: God raises heaven and places the balance; the ayah brings the elevated roof and measured order together just as the section joins sky and a balanced soul.

luna: After sky and balance are paired in 55:7, this verse forbids transgressing the balance, carrying the section's proportion image into a stated limit. | terra: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا فِي الْمِيزَانِ turns the balance placed beside the raised heaven in 55:7 into a norm for human conduct.

luna: The next verse commands a just measure; it gives the balance in 55:7 a concrete human practice, a bridge from formed proportion to measure. | terra: The command to establish weight justly continues the movement from the cosmic balance of 55:7 to balanced human action.

luna: “وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ” continues the raised-heaven scene with earth laid out for living creatures, the floor beneath that roof. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ lays earth down for its inhabitants beneath the raised heaven of 55:7.
luna: The earth laid out in 55:10 is shown bearing fruit and date palms; this verse continues the ground-as-floor image with its produce.
luna: This next verse adds grain and fragrant plants to the produce on the earth laid out in 55:10.

luna: The sky splits and turns rose-like at the judgment boundary, a further specific reversal of the section's ordered ceiling. | terra: The raised heaven of 55:7 will later split and change appearance, marking the end of the balanced structure described earlier in the same surah.
terra: The earth is shaken violently, reversing the stability of the floor spread and prepared for its occupants.
terra: The mountains are pulverized after the earth's shaking in 56:4, removing the peg-like elements along with the floor's stability.
terra: وَظِلٍّ مَمْدُودٍ presents extended shade as part of the garden's prepared dwelling, a positive realization of the sheltering-canopy sense.
luna: The section's roof and shade imply a sheltering cover; this passage's “ظِلٍّ مِّن يَحْمُومٍ” is a smoky shade in punishment.
luna: The next verse says that shade is neither cool nor noble, explicitly reversing the comfort suggested by an overhead shelter.
terra: God can replace people with their likes and produce them in a form or state they do not know, setting the present human build within His power to refashion it.
terra: The names Creator, Originator, and Fashioner identify divine forming itself as an attribute, clarifying the agent behind the section's repeated construction and proportioning verbs.
terra: People standing in a compact rank are كَأَنَّهُمْ بُنْيَانٌ مَرْصُوصٌ; living human parts become a tightly joined building, concretizing the source definition of bināʾ as joining parts.

luna: The verse places the true creation of heaven and earth beside God's shaping humans and making their forms good, bringing the cosmic and human structures together. | terra: Creation of the heavens and earth is immediately joined to God's fashioning human beings well, supporting the section's move from the cosmic house to its human structure.

luna: Seven heavens and matching earths are created together; the verse expands the section's paired upper and lower cosmic structures into a corresponding set. | terra: Seven heavens and a corresponding earth are created, with the command descending among them, making the cosmic enclosure layered and governed from within.

luna: The layered heavens “طِبَاقًا” have no disparity in their creation, a specific account of the sky's ordered construction. | terra: The seven layered heavens show no disparity in the Merciful's creation, echoing the section's completed, flaw-free form and 50:6's unbroken roof.

luna: The inspection of the layered heavens ends with “مِن فُطُورٍ”; this verse sharpens the gapless-roof claim begun in 67:3. | terra: Repeated sight returns unable to find a flaw in the heavens of 67:3, making the roof's finished integrity an examined fact rather than a bare assertion.
terra: The nearest heaven is adorned with lamps that also serve against devils, combining the roof's beauty with active protection.

luna: The earth is made “ذَلُولًا” for walking over; this is a specific inhabited-ground counterpart to the section's spread floor. | terra: Earth is made ذَلُولًا so its inhabitants can walk its slopes and eat God's provision, showing the floor fitted for use rather than merely spread.
terra: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one blow, dismantling both the floor and its peg-like fixtures.

luna: The sky splits open at the judgment boundary, reversing the section's built and unbroken ceiling. | terra: Heaven splits and becomes وَاهِيَةٌ on that day, the direct future reversal of the intact, protected ceiling in the section.
luna: The sky becomes like molten metal; this reverses the section's firm roof into a changed, unstable upper surface.

luna: The heavens are described as “طِبَاقًا,” layered above; this supplies a stacked-ceiling image alongside the section's roof. | terra: The question whether people see how God created seven heavens in layers repeats the image of a deliberately built, tiered overhead structure.
terra: God causes human beings to grow from earth like vegetation, making the third living structure arise from the house's lower member.
terra: People are returned into earth and brought out again after the growth of 71:17, setting a boundary and renewal for the earth-born self.

luna: “الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا” directly names the earth as a spread, carpet-like surface, matching the section's floor and rug senses. | terra: وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا explicitly calls earth a carpet spread for human beings.
luna: After earth is called a spread in 71:19, this verse names broad routes through it; it adds movement across the surface.
terra: The jinn find heaven filled with strong guards and flames, reporting from another speaker's stance how the protected upper boundary is experienced.
terra: The jinn explain that former listening posts at heaven are now met by a waiting flame, specifying the experienced consequence of the strong guards reported in 72:8.

luna: The judgment scene says the sky will split open, another specific boundary to the intact roof. | terra: السَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ makes the promised Day capable of rending the roof, a boundary to its present protection.
terra: The human doubts that God will gather his bones, making bodily reconstruction explicitly a matter of joining the structure's separated parts.
terra: God answers that He can proportion even the fingertips, joining reassembly of the bones in 75:3 to exact finishing of the smallest bodily detail.
terra: The human begins as an emitted drop and then a clot, providing the material sequence that 75:38 completes with خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى.

luna: The verse says the human becomes a clot, then “فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى”; the same root links a formed body to the section's nafs, though this passage emphasizes embryonic sequence. | terra: From the clot introduced by 75:37, فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes human creation culminate in the same act of proportioning used for the section's soul.
terra: After the fashioning of 75:38, God makes the human pair male and female, showing one consequence of that fitted form.
terra: Humanity is made from نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ, a mixed drop, and furnished with hearing and sight, a concrete joining and fitting of capacities.
terra: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ describes God creating people and strengthening their bodily bonds or frame, close to the section's parts joined into a sound build.
terra: وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ فُرِجَتْ opens the sky, reversing the no-fissure ceiling of 50:6.
terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا depicts earth as a containing or gathering place, an additional function of the house's lower surface.
terra: أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا specifies that the earth of 77:25 gathers both living and dead occupants.

luna: The condemned are sent toward a shade with three branches; this turns the section's overhead shade image into a threatening cover. | terra: The command to go to a three-branched "shade" erects a false canopy whose failure to shade or protect is stated in 77:31.

luna: The next verse says that shade neither protects from flame nor shelters; its own contribution is the explicit failure of a covering to shelter. | terra: The three-branched shade introduced at 77:30 is لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ, explicitly denying both shade and protection that define the section's canopy.
luna: “الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا” makes the earth a spread bed, the lower surface in the section's tent-like house. | terra: Calling earth مِهَادًا gives the cosmic house its prepared lower bedding.

luna: “وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا” gives mountains the tent-peg role that the section explicitly derives from its earth-and-tent image. | terra: Mountains as أَوْتَادًا supply the pegs beside the earth-bedding of 78:6, making the section's tent reading concrete.

luna: “وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا” explicitly describes the heavens above as built, matching the section's ceiling structure. | terra: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا depicts the heavens as seven strong structures built directly above the occupants.
terra: The heaven that 78:12 calls a strong built structure will be opened into gates, an internal reversal in the same surah.
luna: The same surah that calls mountains “pegs” in 78:7 later says they are set moving; the tent's fixed anchors are removed at judgment.

luna: The section quotes this challenge to resurrection: “أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ”; the sky's building is set against human creation as evidence for the Creator's power. | terra: The challenge to human beings asks whether they or heaven are harder to create and answers بَنَاهَا, explicitly comparing the human structure with the built sky.

luna: “رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا” completes the roof image and uses the same root س و ي that the section traces from sky to soul. | terra: Within the construction begun at 79:27, God raises the sky's thickness and فَسَوَّاهَا; the same finishing verb that the section applies to the soul finishes the roof.
luna: Between the leveled sky and spread earth, this verse darkens night and brings out daylight; it adds the sky's alternation to the same creation sequence.

luna: “وَالْأَرْضَ ... دَحَاهَا” continues the creation sequence with a spread earth, paired with the raised, leveled sky in 79:28. | terra: After the roof of 79:27-28, earth is دَحَاهَا; the source section explicitly identifies dahw as the parallel of its tahw, so this completes the same roof-and-floor sequence.
luna: Following the earth's spreading in 79:30, this verse brings its water and pasture forth; it shows what the laid-out ground yields.
luna: “وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا” follows the spread earth with fixed mountains, a functional counterpart to the section's tent-pegs.
luna: The next verse names the earth's yield as provision for people and livestock, completing the usable-ground scene begun in 79:30.
terra: مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ presents the human as created and precisely apportioned, clarifying the measured fitness implied by the section's balancing.
terra: When the mountains are set moving, the fixtures associated with holding the earthly tent cease to stand in place.

luna: The sky is stripped away; this gives a distinct removal of the overhead cover imagined as a roof. | terra: وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ pictures the sky stripped away, exposing the eventual removal of the cosmic canopy.

luna: The section's built roof is said to have no fissures, while this judgment scene says “السَّمَاءُ انفَطَرَتْ”; the same sky becomes split. | terra: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْفَطَرَتْ directly reverses the roof with no fissures by showing it split open at the final event.

luna: Addressing each person, God says “خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ”; it directly echoes the section's formed and balanced nafs. | terra: خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ addresses the human directly as created, finished, and balanced, exactly the section's reading of the soul's سَوَّاهَا.

luna: “فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ ... رَكَّبَكَ” describes God assembling a person in a chosen form, a concrete parallel to the section's built human frame. | terra: فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ completes 82:7 by describing the human as assembled into a chosen form, matching building as joining parts.

luna: This is another specific reversal of the section's intact roof: “السَّمَاءُ انشَقَّتْ” at the end-time boundary. | terra: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انْشَقَّتْ places the obedient sky's splitting at the end of its present architectural order.

luna: The earth is stretched out at the final boundary, a specific alteration of the section's spread ground. | terra: وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ repeats the act of extending earth in an eschatological setting, turning the created floor into the surface prepared for final disclosure.
terra: The command that the human look at what he was created from frames 86:6-7 as an inspection of the bodily structure's origin.
terra: Creation from an ejected fluid supplies the living body's generative material before 86:7 locates its emergence within the torso.

luna: The section's building-root dictionary entry calls the ribs of the chest “البواني”; “بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ وَالتَّرَائِبِ” names the back and ribs in the human frame. | terra: The fluid emerges from between the backbone and التَّرَائِبِ, the chest or breastbones, meeting the source dictionary's image of the body's ribs as house-poles without requiring the terms to be identical.

luna: “خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى” repeats the section's key finishing verb, here for the Creator's act of making creation proportionate. | terra: الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوَّى makes creation followed by fitting completion a general signature of the Lord praised here.

luna: The next verse says the Creator “قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى”; its own contribution is measured guidance, extending 87:2's proportioned creation toward the section's balanced design. | terra: وَالَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَى follows creation and proportioning in 87:2 with measure and guidance, showing what fitted completion enables.
terra: وَزَرَابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ supplies literal spread carpets just before 88:18-20 asks the reader to see the raised sky and spread earth.
terra: The question كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ directs sight to heaven as an elevated overhead structure.
terra: Mountains are set upright between the raised sky of 88:18 and spread earth of 88:20; read with 78:7, they function as the scene's structural pegs.

luna: “وَإِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ” directs attention to the earth as a spread surface, the section's lower floor. | terra: The question كَيْفَ سُطِحَتْ presents earth as a laid-out surface beneath the raised sky of 88:18.
terra: دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا crushes the spread floor flat at judgment, reversing its present settled use.

luna: “الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ” specifically presents the human form as excellently proportioned, matching the section's completed nafs structure. | terra: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ states the human result as the finest formed constitution, parallel to the section's flawless sawiyy form.
